triage_reason: Blind Hunter, map shows only the current page: decision-needed. The spec intent says "filtered listings", so whether the map should cover all results is a product call.

description: The map is a plain gradient with no geographic context. Pin positions shift with the filters, MIN_SPAN is applied in degrees after the mercator transform, and overlapping pins or an edge overflow are not handled.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, plain gradient map and pin geometry: defer. A real tile map is out of scope for this story, and overlapping pins are cosmetic.

description: Accessibility gaps: no `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls` on pins, the preview is not announced, focus is not returned on close, Escape is bound to the whole document, and the close button is a tiny "×".
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, accessibility gaps: patch. Add `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` to pins, announce the preview, return focus to the pin on close, and scope Escape to the map.

description: A hard-coded "→" in the link text and a duplicate "Map" label (`Search.view.map` and `Search.map.showMap`) go against the spec rule that all strings come from the message catalog.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, hard-coded "→" and duplicate "Map" label: patch. Minor, but it breaks the all-strings-via-catalog rule.

description: The mobile in-page List/Map tabs sit next to the server Grid/Map toggle, which is confusing.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, two toggles on mobile: defer. This is a UX design question, not a defect.

description: Test gaps: no test that the client-side `router.push` path keeps `view`, the "invalid view" test does not check toggle state, the mobile pane assertion on class names is fragile, and the `page` reset on switching views is untested.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, test gaps: patch. Add the client `router.push` test (the same gap as the Verification Gap entry below) and tighten the invalid-view and class-name assertions.

description: The type says `number` but numeric strings are accepted, and empty strings and the 0/0 "null island" are not rejected.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, coordinate typing and validation: patch. Reject blank strings and booleans, and align the type with the validation. Merge this with the Edge Case Hunter whitespace finding.

description: A stale `selectedId` is not cleared when the listing leaves the page. The mobile default pane is "map", and `priority` is dropped on the first card images.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, stale `selectedId`, default pane, `priority`: patch for the stale `selectedId` (same fix as the Edge Case Hunter entry below). Defer the `priority` and default-pane points.

description: Spec hygiene: Implementation Notes, Verification and Tasks are empty or unchecked while the status is `review`, with no test or build evidence.
triage_reason: Blind Hunter, spec hygiene: defer. The notes and task checkboxes are process artifacts to fill in at closure.

description: `Math.min(...xs)` spread could throw `RangeError` on very large arrays. The page size of 12 makes this negligible.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, `Math.min` spread: reject. Page size is 12, so there is no real risk.

description: A whitespace-only string or a boolean passes `Number()` as finite, so a pin lands at the equator.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, whitespace or boolean coordinates: patch. It is a one-line guard and a real misplacement bug.

description: A stale `selectedId` stays set after the listing leaves the page. The preview is hidden but the ring highlight is orphaned, and the selection returns later.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, stale `selectedId`: patch. Clear the selection when the listing is no longer in `pins`.

description: The document-level Escape handler closes the preview even when the key press belongs to another widget.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, global Escape: patch. Scope it to the map or ignore `defaultPrevented` events.

description: The mobile pane defaults to "map". With JS disabled or before hydration the list is hidden and the tabs do nothing.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, mobile default "map" before hydration: decision-needed. Defaulting to the list would be safer without JS, but the choice is a product call.

description: `next/image` in the preview may fail for hosts not in `remotePatterns`, and there is no `onError` fallback.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, `next/image` hosts: defer. It is the same image setup the rest of the app uses, so it is unlikely to be new here.

description: A null or non-numeric `price_cop` renders "COP NaN" in the pin and the aria-label.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, null `price_cop`: reject. The column is NOT NULL and the existing cards already format it the same way.

description: Pins with identical or near-identical coordinates stack exactly, so the lower pin cannot be reached.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, stacked pins: defer. Clustering is out of scope for this story.

description: The preview card covers the bottom of the canvas and can hide the lowest pins while it is open.
triage_reason: Edge Case Hunter, preview covers lowest pins: defer. Minor layout polish.

description: No test checks that filter changes keep `view=map` through the client `router.push` path.
triage_reason: Verification Gap, no `view=map` test on the client push path: patch. Add the `routerPush` test in `SearchFilters.test.tsx`; this is the same point as finding 8.

description: No test pins the `select("*")` that supplies the coordinate columns. This is a regression risk only if the select is narrowed later.
triage_reason: Verification Gap, no test pins the select: defer. It is a regression-only risk.

description: The mobile default pane "map" is not mentioned in the spec.
triage_reason: Verification Gap, mobile default pane not in spec: defer. This overlaps with finding 16.

description: `isCoordinate` accepts strings such as "0x10" and " " through `Number()`.
triage_reason: Verification Gap, `isCoordinate` accepts "0x10": reject. It is harmless for PostgREST numerics, and finding 13 already covers the real case.

description: The toggle uses `aria-current` where the spec matrix says "pressed", with no `aria-pressed`.
triage_reason: Acceptance Auditor, `aria-current` instead of pressed: reject. The links are navigation, so `aria-current` is the correct semantics.

description: The map shows only the paginated page, not all filtered results, which is arguably against the intent.
triage_reason: Acceptance Auditor, map shows only the paginated page: decision-needed. This duplicates finding 3.

description: A stale `selectedId` persists when the mobile pane switches or the page changes.
triage_reason: Acceptance Auditor, `selectedId` persists across the pane switch: reject. The selection should survive a pane switch, and the stale-page case is finding 14.

description: The extra `Search.map` keys (`paneLabel`, `showList`, `showMap`) are not in the spec, but the en and es catalogs are in parity.
triage_reason: Acceptance Auditor, extra `Search.map` keys: reject. They back the mobile tabs, both catalogs are in parity, and it is informational only.

description: The success and error messages have no persistent aria-live region, so assistive tech may not announce them.
triage_reason: defer: Real a11y improvement, but not in the spec and it affects no AC. Fix it together with the other form a11y items.

description: The form ships against a nonexistent /api/newsletter, with no flag or TODO, no contract test, and one generic error for 400/409/429.
triage_reason: defer: The spec says the endpoint is S13 and the form shows the error state until then. The error-code handling belongs to S13.

description: Consent is never recorded server-side (no timestamp or policy version), and the consent copy has no privacy-policy link.
triage_reason: defer: The spec says consent is client-side only. Server-side recording and the policy link belong to S13 (policies).

description: There is no honeypot, rate limiting or captcha, no locale is sent, and validation is client-only.
triage_reason: defer: Server-side protection belongs to S13.

description: The aria-labelledby ids (newsletter-title, testimonials-title, resources-title) are hard-coded and could collide.
triage_reason: reject: Each id is used once per page, and the sections render once.

description: Inputs have no required or aria-required, and the aria-hidden "*" hides that fields are required from screen readers.
triage_reason: patch: Adding `required` and `aria-required` is cheap and the "*" is otherwise meaningless to screen readers. `noValidate` is fine, but the fields need to be announced as required.

description: Focus is not moved to the first invalid field after a failed validation.
triage_reason: defer: Focus management on error is an a11y nicety outside the spec.

description: The aria-invalid red border is low contrast on the dark background.
triage_reason: reject: The red-500 border sits alongside red text and an error message, so it is not the sole cue.

description: A stale error or success status is not cleared when the user edits a field.
triage_reason: patch: Clearing the status on edit is a small change that fixes the stale banner.

description: EMAIL_RE is too loose or too strict for some addresses (single-label domains, odd forms).
triage_reason: defer: The lenient regex is a deliberate trade-off, and the server validates in S13.

description: The validation tests are thin: no IDN, plus-address or trailing-dot cases, the 250-character local part is invalid anyway, and the 200-character name limit is not tested exactly.
triage_reason: reject: The test inputs are valid for their purpose, and the exact-limit coverage is nitpicking.

description: The testimonials are fabricated placeholder quotes with real-sounding names, presented as genuine reviews with no "sample" marker.
triage_reason: decision-needed: Fabricated testimonials are a product and legal call. They need a "sample" label or real content.

description: The resource cards look clickable but have no link or "coming soon" label, and no date, author or image.
triage_reason: reject: This matches the spec notes (non-linked articles), and the content is intentional.

description: There is no test for the double-submit guard, for clearing success on re-edit, for aria-describedby wiring, or for Home page integration.
triage_reason: defer: Extra test coverage, and the double-submit guard is low risk.

description: One test file covers three components under a name that fits none of them, and the listitem and label queries are loose.
triage_reason: reject: A style nitpick about test file organization.

description: The spec status is `done` while sprint-status.yaml says `review`.
triage_reason: patch: The spec and sprint status should agree. This is a metadata fix only.

description: The spec says the blind-hunter layer was skipped, and its "314 passed" claim has no committed evidence.
triage_reason: reject: This is process noise and does not affect the code.

description: The fetch has no timeout or AbortController, so a stalled request leaves the button disabled on "Subscribing…".
triage_reason: defer: A timeout or AbortController is robustness work that fits with the S13 integration.

description: A 409 or other 4xx for an already-subscribed email shows a generic failure.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate handling depends on the S13 API contract.

description: Focus stays on the submit button after a failed validation, so the errors are not announced.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 7.

description: The success banner stays after the user edits the fields or resubmits.
triage_reason: patch: Same fix as item 9, since it is the same stale-state defect.

description: The role=status/alert elements are mounted with their text already inside, so some assistive tech does not announce them.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 1.

description: The regex accepts a..b@x.com, a@-x.com and a@x.c.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 10.

description: Consent is not included in the POST payload.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 3, and the spec documents it.

description: The quote marks are hard-coded in JSX instead of coming from the locale files.
triage_reason: reject: Typographic quote marks are not translatable copy, and the spec's i18n constraint targets user-facing strings.

description: The in-flight double submit and the success-then-resubmit path are untested.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 14.

description: The spec says `done` and sprint-status says `review`.
triage_reason: reject: Duplicate of finding 16.

description: The "all strings via next-intl" claim is not literally true (hard-coded quote marks and "*"), and the parity test covers only three sections.
triage_reason: reject: Same as finding 25. The claim is fine in practice.

description: The Home page has no test that it composes Testimonials, ResourceCards and NewsletterForm, so removing them would not fail any test.
triage_reason: defer: Low-risk static composition, so a Home page test can be added later.

description: The test pins the POST body to exactly {name, email}, which fixes "consent not sent" and would fail if S13 changes the contract.
triage_reason: defer: The test deliberately pins the current contract and gets updated in S13.

description: The section and the form both use aria-labelledby="newsletter-title", so two landmarks share one name.
triage_reason: reject: Both are named by the same title, so the landmark is not a real issue.

description: The /Name/, /Email/, /Nombre/ and /Correo/ label queries are loose and rely on the " *" suffix.
triage_reason: reject: The loose queries pass and carry no real risk.

description: No test checks that the success message clears when the user edits again.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 14.

description: Until S13 ships the endpoint 404s, so the form always shows the error state, and tests mock fetch only.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 2, and expected until S13.

description: The spec's "314 passed" and clean-build claims are unverified in the diff, and its `done` status conflicts with sprint-status `review`.
triage_reason: reject: Duplicate of finding 16.

description: The server has no proof of consent, which may conflict with S13 (policies), although the spec documents this as intentional.
triage_reason: defer: Duplicate of finding 3, and the spec documents it.

description: The success branch does not check the response type, so a non-JSON or opaque 200 counts as success.
